title: Every automated test gets an outcome
statement: assure record MUST write an outcome for every test record whose state is automated in the spec at the commit, and MUST record a test that did not run as failed with the detail did not run.

title: Outcomes are keyed by the test's ID
statement: assure record MUST take each outcome from the runners' machine-readable output by the lathe ID the test carries in its name, for Go subtests and Python subtests alike, and MUST ignore a test whose name carries no ID.

title: An unknown ID refuses the run
statement: assure record MUST exit non-zero and write no predicate when an outcome names an ID that is not a test record in the spec at the commit.

title: The subject is the exact commit
statement: The proof run's subject MUST be the full commit CI checked out, and assure record MUST refuse a tree with uncommitted changes.

title: The provider signs and keeps it
statement: The proof run MUST be signed by the provider's trusted signer through the provider's attestation action and kept by the provider, and CI MUST NOT commit it or any evidence file to the repository.

title: No obligation falls
statement: assure judge change MUST refuse a change under which any obligation present at the base branch's head is no longer designed, built or proved, and MUST NOT refuse a change only because it adds obligations that are not yet built or proved.

title: Every proof passed at the change's commit
statement: assure judge change MUST refuse a change whose commit has no verified proof run, or whose proof run has an automated test record not passed.

title: A refusal names every cause
statement: assure judge change MUST name each obligation that fell, with the share it fell from, and each test record that did not pass, and MUST exit non-zero.

title: The verdict is reproducible
statement: assure judge change MUST give the same verdict and reasons for the same commit, base and proof run, in the same order.

title: Every share is 100%
statement: assure judge release MUST refuse a release commit whose designed, built or proved share is below 100%, and MUST name each obligation that is not.

title: A passed proof run at the release commit
statement: assure judge release MUST refuse a release commit with no verified proof run, or with any automated test record not passed there.

title: A passed verdict is attested
statement: A passed release verdict MUST be signed by the provider's trusted signer with the release commit as subject and kept by the provider, so release qualification can verify it.

title: The ledger comes from attestations alone
statement: assure ledger MUST build its view from attestations it verified and from the spec at the commit, and MUST read no evidence file from the repository.

title: Each test record shows where it last passed
statement: assure ledger MUST show, for each test record, its state at the commit, its result there, and the newest commit a verified proof run passed it at.

title: An unverifiable attestation shows as none
statement: assure ledger MUST show no result for a commit whose attestation fails verification, and MUST say why.

title: Module files change only on success
statement: stego deps MUST change go.mod and go.sum only after resolution and its checks succeed, and a failed or interrupted run MUST leave both as they were or recoverable through stego recover.

title: Resolution follows the captured source
statement: stego deps MUST resolve only the source STEGO captured, whatever Go settings the environment or the Go configuration file holds.

title: Resolution waits for generation
statement: stego deps MUST refuse while the generated code is out of date with its declaration, and name the run to make first.

title: A cache holds exactly what go.sum states
statement: stego build download MUST store only module zips whose hashes go.sum states, and MUST refuse a zip that differs.

title: A cache is recorded
statement: stego build download MUST write a record that lists each module by path, version and hash, and the source revision it serves.

title: A build needs no network
statement: stego build MUST run with the network off, from a recorded module cache, and MUST fail when a module is missing or differs from go.sum.

title: A build uses the archetype's toolchain
statement: stego build MUST use the Go SDK that the service's archetype pins, checked by digest, and MUST refuse any other SDK.

title: Two builds give the same bytes
statement: stego build MUST build twice and MUST fail unless both builds give byte-identical executables; a later build from the same inputs MUST give the same bytes again.

title: The record names every input and output
statement: stego build MUST write a build record that names the source revision, the Go SDK, the module cache, the build settings, the generation record, the executable digest, and an SPDX and a CycloneDX SBOM.

title: Only a trusted record counts
statement: Every check MUST take the record's digest from verified provenance and MUST refuse a record whose canonical bytes do not hash to it.

title: A check names every difference
statement: A check MUST fail when any digest the record names differs, and MUST name each one.

title: An image comes only from a trusted build
statement: stego image build MUST refuse an executable whose digest a trusted build record does not name, and a CA bundle whose digest is not trusted; it MUST NOT read the host's trust store.

title: An image is scratch and the same each time
statement: stego image build MUST build on scratch, run as a non-root user, and give the same image digest from the same build record, executable and CA bundle.

title: The provider's trusted signer signs image and SBOMs
statement: An image and its SPDX and CycloneDX SBOM attestations MUST be signed by the trusted signer the service's delivery pipeline names for the provider that built it, and verification MUST accept only that identity.

title: Publication is exact and explicit
statement: stego image publish MUST push only a verified image, to an explicit repository over TLS with an explicit CA and credentials, and MUST read the image back and refuse a registry that holds different bytes.

title: A retrieved image is checked before use
statement: stego image retrieve MUST check the pulled image against its record, its trusted build record and its signature before it writes the image anywhere.

title: A scaffold is accepted as written
statement: The declaration STEGO scaffolds MUST pass checking with no change to it.

title: A scaffold overwrites nothing
statement: Scaffolding MUST refuse to run when a declaration is already present, and MUST NOT change or remove any existing file.

title: An unknown archetype is refused with the choices
statement: Scaffolding MUST refuse an archetype the registry does not hold, and MUST name the archetypes it does hold.

title: Example content is the smallest that passes
statement: The example content a scaffold writes MUST be the smallest content that checking accepts for that archetype.

title: An empty scaffold names what it owes
statement: When the author asks for a scaffold with no example content, STEGO MUST leave that content out, and MUST name every setting the author must supply at the time it writes the scaffold.

title: Init resolves the registry as generation does
statement: stego init MUST resolve the registry with the same resolver and rules as generation, MUST hold the apply lock, MUST keep the configuration bytes as written, MUST refuse a symbolic link at any path it would write, and when no configuration exists MUST write one that names ./registry, or the environment override, as a local source.

title: The report covers every input of the active set
statement: The report MUST name every component of the active component set, every setting each component declares with its type, and every slot each component declares.

title: The report is structured data
statement: The report MUST be available as structured data, so an agent can read it without parsing prose.

title: The report and the check cannot disagree
statement: The report MUST come from the same declarations that checking reads, so a declaration the report allows MUST NOT be refused as undeclared.

title: The report exposes what checking enforces
statement: The report MUST expose every allowed value and every optional flag that checking enforces, so a value the report presents as allowed MUST NOT be refused.

title: Checking writes nothing
statement: Checking MUST NOT create, change or remove any file, whether it accepts the declaration or refuses it.

title: Every fault at once
statement: A refusal MUST report every fault STEGO can find, and MUST NOT stop at the first one.

title: One checking stage
statement: STEGO MUST check a declaration against one set of rules, so generation MUST NOT refuse a declaration that checking accepted.

title: An expired acceptance is named
statement: When an acceptance is past its date, checking MUST fail and MUST name the component, the date and the successor stage it waits for.

title: A fault is structured data
statement: Each fault MUST be available as structured data, and MUST NOT be available only as prose for a person.

title: A fault names its rule and its place
statement: Each fault MUST name the rule it breaks and the path in the declaration where STEGO found it.

title: A fault names the allowed values
statement: When the rule a fault breaks allows a stated set of values, the fault MUST name that set.

title: Prose is a rendering of the fault
statement: The prose STEGO prints for a person MUST be rendered from the structured fault, so the two MUST NOT disagree.

title: The query answers from records alone
statement: The query MUST answer from the committed records alone, with no network call and no service to operate.

title: A missing record is reported
statement: When a searched checkout holds generated output with no record, the query MUST report it as unknown and MUST NOT omit it from the result.

title: The answer names version and digest
statement: The report MUST name each affected service with both the version and the digest of the component it holds.

title: A fix carries no unrelated changes
statement: A component content fix MUST reach a consumer without forcing that consumer to take any change unrelated to the fix.

title: A successor is declared, never inferred
statement: The registry MUST record each superseded component digest with its successor digest and the date after which the superseded digest fails.

title: A breaking change is declared
statement: A supersession record MUST state whether taking the successor needs a change to the service declaration or to a fill, because a digest carries no compatibility meaning of its own.

title: The compiler pin and the registry pin move apart
statement: The compiler pin and the registry pin MUST move independently of each other, within a compatibility range the registry declares.

title: A runtime fix ships the same way
statement: A fix in the runtime library MUST reach a service as a component fix does: a new tagged version, the archetype's pin moved to it, the old version recorded as superseded with a fail date, and each consumer taking it by a registry pin bump and a new run; a consumer MUST NOT be able to take it by editing go.mod.

title: Superseded warns and does not block
statement: Validate and plan MUST report every pinned component digest that the registry records as superseded, and MUST NOT fail for that reason alone.

title: The report names the successor and the date
statement: Each report of a superseded pin MUST name the successor digest and the date after which the pin fails.

title: Past its date a pin fails unless overridden
statement: After the stated date, validate MUST fail for that pin, and apply MUST NOT write output unless the author overrides that pin by name, as Generating records it.

title: An unread registry is not a pass
statement: When STEGO cannot read the registry's supersession records, it MUST report that it could not check and MUST NOT report the pins as current.

title: A withdrawal names its consumers first
statement: Before a withdrawal takes effect, STEGO MUST be able to name every recorded service that pins the withdrawn digest.

title: A withdrawal carries a future date
statement: A withdrawal MUST carry the date after which the digest fails, and STEGO MUST refuse a withdrawal whose date is already past.

title: A withdrawn digest takes no new pin
statement: STEGO MUST refuse a new pin to a withdrawn digest at once, whatever date the withdrawal carries.

title: Qualification is at one exact commit
statement: Qualification MUST verify the compiler checks and the signed artifacts at the exact commit the release names, and MUST NOT accept a result from a descendant or an ancestor.

title: A missing result is not a pass
statement: Qualification MUST require a conclusion for every required job, and MUST treat a missing result as a failure.

title: The published release is verified as a consumer sees it
statement: Qualification MUST authenticate the published release through the same path a consumer uses, and MUST cross-check every published asset digest against the qualified artifacts.

title: A release carries a passed release verdict
statement: Qualification MUST verify a passed release verdict attested at exactly the commit under qualification, by the provider's trusted signer, and MUST fail when there is none.

title: The qualified platform is stated and enforced
statement: An installation MUST state the platform the release is qualified for, and MUST refuse to install on any other platform.

title: Identity is verified before the binary is used
statement: The installer MUST verify the artifact signature and digest before it puts the binary in place.

title: The compiler reports the identity it records
statement: The installed compiler MUST report the same build identity that it writes into a service's record.

title: Every need is stated
statement: stego apply MUST write platform-requirements.yaml that states every secret with its keys, configuration value, database, topic, identity issuer, ingress, egress endpoint with its port, cluster permission and pod security level the service's components need.

title: No environment values
statement: platform-requirements.yaml MUST NOT hold a secret value, a host name, an address, a namespace or any other value that differs per environment.

title: The same declaration gives the same file
statement: stego apply MUST write the same platform-requirements.yaml for the same declaration and registry.

title: Every unmet need is named
statement: stego env check MUST name every requirement the environment file does not meet, with what is missing, and MUST exit non-zero when one is unmet.

title: Values are typed
statement: stego env check MUST refuse a value of the wrong type, such as an image named by tag instead of digest or a secret without a key the requirement names.

title: The check reads names only
statement: stego env check MUST read secret names and keys only, never secret values, and MUST change nothing.

title: The CI file is one pinned call
statement: stego apply MUST write a CI file that only calls the provider's shared pipeline and the STEGO checks by pinned references: the platform's reusable workflow by commit SHA for GitHub Actions, or the Konflux standard pipeline bundle by digest for Konflux.

title: Every STEGO check runs on every provider
statement: Each provider's pipeline MUST run drift, vet, test, a reproducible stego build and the executable match, and MUST NOT release an image for delivery when any of them fails.

title: A Konflux image holds the recorded executable
statement: stego delivery check MUST refuse an image whose executable differs by one byte from the executable its stego build record names.

title: The Containerfile builds offline
statement: The generated Containerfile MUST build on scratch with the network off, from Konflux's prefetched modules, with the archetype's Go SDK and the settings stego build uses.

title: The provider's trusted signer signs
statement: An image MUST be signed by its provider's trusted signer only: the pinned workflow's keyless identity on GitHub Actions, or the Tekton Chains key on Konflux.

title: The pin comes from the registry
statement: stego apply MUST take every pinned reference and trusted signer from the registry's ci-pipeline component, and MUST NOT let service.yaml override them.

title: A patch changes only the pin
statement: A new ci-pipeline version that changes only a pin MUST change only that pin in each regenerated CI file.

title: An unpinned reference is refused
statement: stego apply MUST refuse a ci-pipeline component whose reference uses a tag, a branch or a short SHA.

title: The base needs no plugin
statement: stego apply MUST write a Kubernetes base that plain kustomize builds, with no plugin, generator program or remote base.

title: The base holds no environment values
statement: The Kubernetes base MUST NOT set replicas, a PodDisruptionBudget, a namespace, an image digest, a host name, an egress address or a secret value.

title: The base carries what service.yaml derives
statement: The Kubernetes base MUST carry the probes health-check derives and default resource requests and limits that an overlay may change.

title: The delivery object holds no environment values
statement: stego apply MUST write an Argo CD Application from the delivery stanza that names the service, its project and its base, and takes its destination and overlay from the platform.

title: An environment is checked before it is applied
statement: The platform's GitOps flow MUST run stego env check on an environment file, and Argo CD MUST NOT apply an overlay whose check fails.

title: The scaffold compiles against the contract
statement: stego fill create MUST write a fill whose code compiles against the slot's contract and a test file that runs, and MUST NOT overwrite an existing fill.

title: A fill binds only to the slot it implements
statement: Generation MUST refuse a binding whose fill implements another slot or serves another collection, and MUST name the fill, the slot and the collection.

title: A fill imports only what it may
statement: STEGO MUST record no evidence for a fill that imports anything but its slot's contract, the standard library and the modules the declaration lists for fills, and MUST name the import.

title: A fill without tests cannot ship
statement: Generation MUST refuse a bound fill that holds no test file, and MUST name it.

title: Passing tests leave evidence
statement: stego test MUST write, into each fill's fill.yaml, evidence that its tests passed, with the fill's content digest and its contract's digest, and MUST write none for a fill whose tests fail.

title: Only a listed key qualifies a fill
statement: stego fill sign MUST sign the current evidence with the person's SSH or GPG key, and generation MUST accept only a signature by a key that the project's SIGNERS file lists.

title: A signature covers one evidence
statement: A sign-off MUST sign the digest of the evidence it covers, so it cannot be moved to other evidence or to another fill.

title: STEGO never signs by itself
statement: STEGO MUST NOT create, store or use a signing key of its own; a sign-off MUST come from a key the person holds.

title: The catalog shows each fill with its standing
statement: stego registry fills MUST list each fill in the project that implements the slot, with its collection and its qualification standing.

title: A change makes a fill stale
statement: When a fill's code, its tests or its slot contract changes after its evidence was recorded, STEGO MUST report the fill as stale, and generation MUST refuse it.

title: The report says what changed
statement: For each fill that is not qualified, stego fill status MUST name the fill and why: no tests, no evidence, no sign-off, an unlisted key, or the file or contract that changed.

title: Requalifying needs new evidence and a new signature
statement: A stale fill MUST become qualified again only through new evidence and a new sign-off of that evidence; its old sign-off MUST NOT carry over.

title: The record names every input digest
statement: Apply MUST write a record that names the service, the compiler digest, the registry digest, and the digest and version of every component it used.

title: No output without a record
statement: STEGO MUST NOT leave generated output in place without the record of the inputs that produced it.

title: The record reads without STEGO
statement: The record MUST be a plain text file that a reader can parse without the compiler, so a sweep does not run STEGO in every checkout.

title: The record's format is a stated contract
statement: The record MUST carry its own format version, and STEGO MUST NOT change or remove a documented field of the record without changing that version.

title: The record carries a hash per file
statement: The record MUST carry the hash of every file apply wrote, and the check MUST fail when a file no longer matches its hash.

title: A record that disagrees with state is broken
statement: When the record names a compiler or registry digest that the service's own state does not hold, STEGO MUST report the record as broken rather than trust either one.

title: A fix lands only by regeneration
statement: A component fix MUST reach generated code only through a new generation run, and MUST NOT need a hand edit to any generated file.

title: The diff shows the fix and nothing else
statement: Apply MUST change only the files that the new component digest affects, so the diff a reviewer reads carries the fix alone.

title: A hand edit stops the run unless it is allowed
statement: When a generated file no longer matches its recorded hash, apply MUST report every such file and MUST NOT write, unless the service author states on the command that the run may replace them.

title: A pin that does not stand is refused unless overridden
statement: stego plan and stego apply MUST refuse, and write nothing, when a pin is withdrawn or past its fail date, naming the pin and its successor; the author MAY override one pin by name on the command, and the record MUST then name that pin and the reason, so the fleet sweep shows it.

title: The same inputs give the same code
statement: Two runs from the same declaration, registry content and compiler MUST produce byte-identical files, and a second apply MUST change nothing.

title: Apply removes what it no longer generates
statement: Apply MUST delete each generated file that the record lists and the new plan does not generate. It MUST refuse when that file is hand-edited, as for any other generated file.

title: A failed run changes nothing
statement: When validation, a generator or the assembler fails, the run MUST change no file in the project, and MUST name the failure.

title: Planning writes no generated file
statement: Making a plan MUST write no file in the output folder and MUST NOT change the record. It MUST save the plan only under .stego/.

title: The plan names every change
statement: A plan MUST name every file it would create, update or delete, and whether the record changes.

title: Apply carries out exactly the saved plan
statement: Given a saved plan, apply MUST write exactly the files that the plan names, with the content it planned, or refuse and write nothing.

title: Recovery completes the interrupted apply
statement: Recover MUST complete each write in the journal, so the generated files and the record match the record that the apply was writing.

title: A file changed during the interruption stops recovery
statement: Recover MUST refuse, and change nothing, when a file in the journal matches neither its state before nor its state after the write.

title: The same folder gives the same bundle
statement: stego assets MUST write the same bytes for the same folder, with sorted entries and fixed metadata.

title: A bad entry changes nothing
statement: stego assets MUST check every entry before it writes, and MUST leave the output file as it was when any entry is refused.

title: The view shows all four aspects
statement: stego apply MUST write an architecture view that shows the service's structure, data model, request flows and platform edges.

title: The view opens anywhere
statement: The architecture view MUST be one HTML file that opens in a browser with no server, no network and no external script, style or font.

title: Every element traces to its source
statement: Each element in the view MUST name the declaration entry or registry part it comes from, and the view MUST name the record it was written with.

title: The view is interactive
statement: A reader MUST be able to select any element to see what it connects to, and follow a request flow step by step from its endpoint to its store and the events it raises.

title: The model diff shows each change
statement: stego apply MUST write the architecture model as a sorted, readable data file beside the view, so a review diff shows each element added, removed or changed.

title: A stale view is drift
statement: The drift check MUST fail and name the architecture view or model when either no longer matches the record.

title: A component declares its inputs before it generates
statement: A component MUST declare its config schema, the ports it requires and provides, and the slots it offers, before its generator runs.

title: A claimed namespace is refused twice
statement: STEGO MUST refuse a component whose output namespace another component in the same registry already claims, and MUST name both components.

title: A version moves when the output moves
statement: A component's version MUST change whenever the code its generator emits changes.

title: Each contract names the code and the test
statement: Each thing the emitted code must always do MUST be stated as its own contract, with the code that builds it and the test that proves it named.

title: A component states its architecture role
statement: A component MUST declare its layer, its part in a request flow and the side of each of its ports before the registry accepts it, and the registry MUST refuse one that states none.

title: A component emits no static file
statement: The registry MUST refuse a component, on add and on release, when any file it emits is the same for two declarations that differ in everything it reads, and MUST name the file; such code belongs in the runtime library.

title: A replacement is named and refused
statement: When a local registry supplies a part that the common registry already supplies, STEGO MUST refuse the composition and MUST name the part and both registries.

title: The active set is pinned and recorded
statement: STEGO MUST record the reference of every registry in the active set, so a reader can tell which parts a service was built from.

title: A composition is bounded and whole
statement: STEGO MUST refuse a composition with more than eight sources, with two sources that supply the same artifact name or input path even as identical copies, with a symbolic link in a registry or vendor path, or whose combined inputs exceed 64 MiB or 4,096 files, and MUST capture every source before it validates any.

title: A Git source is pinned and read as pinned
statement: A Git registry source MUST pin a full lower-case commit SHA; a cached or vendored checkout MUST be verified at that commit; and with a vendor path set STEGO MUST read only that checkout, MUST refuse one without Git metadata or with modified, ignored or untracked files, and MUST NOT fetch.

title: Namespaces and pins are checked before any source is read
statement: STEGO MUST refuse a component namespace entry that names a component outside the active set, an empty path or a compiler-owned path; MUST refuse a nonempty per-component pin entry before it resolves any source; and MUST warn when the registry environment override replaces the configured sources.

title: An unanswered port is named
statement: When an archetype leaves a required port with no provider, or with more than one, STEGO MUST refuse the archetype and MUST name the port and every component involved.

title: An experiment on a golden path is named
statement: When an archetype or a mixin includes a component whose stage is not ga, STEGO MUST refuse it and MUST name the component and its stage.

title: A scaffold for the archetype is accepted
statement: An archetype MUST supply the smallest example content that lets a fresh declaration of it pass checking.

title: An experiment states its stage and its clock
statement: A component whose stage is alpha or beta MUST state the date it stops working, and STEGO MUST refuse a date that is already past.

title: An experiment is reachable only on purpose
statement: A service MUST NOT use a component whose stage is not ga unless its declaration accepts that component by name.

title: A request states its outcome, references and promises first
statement: A component MUST be introduced with the business outcome it serves, the best-in-field references it will be compared with or why none exists, and its promise list as output contracts, before its generator is written; STEGO MUST refuse an experimental component that lacks any of the three. An experiment MAY decline a reference's promise, with a reason, but MUST NOT leave one unmentioned.

title: Graduation names its consumers first
statement: Before a component's stage changes, STEGO MUST be able to name every recorded service that uses it.

title: A missed sunset is reported, never silent
statement: When a component passes its sunset date without graduating, STEGO MUST report every service that still uses it, and MUST fail the check for each of them.

title: A ga component carries no clock
statement: A component whose stage is ga MUST NOT state a sunset date.

title: Graduation to ga needs the quality bar
statement: STEGO MUST refuse to move a component to ga unless it holds a security review, a benchmark against a reference and a design review, each at its current digest, and MUST name each missing piece.

title: Graduation to ga needs a current reference comparison
statement: STEGO MUST refuse to move a component to ga unless a reference comparison recorded at the current digest of its contract set leaves no reference promise neither adopted nor declined with a reason, and MUST name each undecided promise.

title: A component is promoted whole and unchanged
statement: Promotion MUST copy the component into the common registry at its exact digest, with its config schema, ports, slots, output contracts and generator, and MUST refuse a component whose name the common registry already holds.

title: A promoted component starts at alpha
statement: A promoted component MUST enter the common registry at stage alpha, whatever its stage was in the local registry, so it climbs the ladder and meets the quality bar under the common registry's rules.

title: Only a reviewed change promotes
statement: A component MUST enter the common registry only through a change to the common registry that a platform engineer reviews and accepts; STEGO MUST NOT write to the common registry by itself.

title: Moving to the promoted component changes no code
statement: When a service moves its pin from the local component to the promoted one, and their digests are the same, regeneration MUST change no generated file.
